I am 51 years old and I have farmed these 7 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags and I sometimes go to the village training meetings when the extension office comes. But honestly, I trust what I see with my own eyes more than anything. I watch my neighbors — if Lao Zhang's wheat looks good, I ask him what seed and fertilizer he used.

This year I will keep my land split the same as last year: 4 mu for wheat-maize rotation and 3 mu for cotton. I don't change this because it has worked. My family has 4 people and some work off-farm, so I can't watch every mu all day. I need a system I know.

For the wheat already in the ground since last fall, I used an improved variety — not the most expensive seed, but the same one I used two years ago when I got good yield. I will topdress with urea at green-up and again at jointing stage. In total I put about 80 jin of urea per mu over the season, plus the compound fertilizer I used at planting. That comes to about 20 kg of pure nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphate, and 5 kg of potash. I will irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I spray twice — once for aphids and once when I see powdery mildew starting. I expect 500 kg per mu if the spring drought doesn't come.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize right away — you have to hurry before the soil dries. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer every year; nobody around here uses saved seed for maize. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting and then topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. That is about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphate, and 5 kg potash. I irrigate twice: once when it's shooting up and once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays — herbicide at seedling stage and insecticide later. I expect 600 kg per mu.

For cotton, I plough deep in April because cotton needs loose soil for the taproot. I plant hybrid Bt cotton — the seed is expensive but I save money on bollworm spray. I use compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea at first flowering. Total is about 15 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphate, and 7 kg potash. Cotton needs water at flowering, boll-setting, and boll-opening, so three irrigations. I spray four times: for aphids, for red spider mite, and twice for leaf diseases. I am hoping for 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 260, so this is my target.

Fertilizer prices worry me. Urea went up 20 yuan per bag from last year. But I would rather spend an extra 100 yuan on fertilizer than lose 200 kg of yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family. My son works off-farm but his income is not steady. The farm is what feeds us. So when I am unsure, I do what I did last year. Change is too risky.
